title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders
abstract: arXiv:2610.32894v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Location encoders map geographic coordinates to high-dimensional descriptors through contrastive alignment with paired Earth Observation imagery. We prove that this construction is structurally limited: any Lipschitz location encoder produces an output of intrinsic dimension at most 2, regardless of architecture or bandwidth, which forces the contrastive loss to strictly exceed its asymptotic optimum. Empirically, joint training also collapses the encoder's embedding covariance to low rank. Although dimension-limited, current location encoders sidestep this spectral collapse by training against a frozen image encoder, which we reinterpret as a covariance regularizer that supplies a high-rank target for the location encoder to fold onto. However, extending this approach to multimodal inputs is challenging, as location encoders should simultaneously map a single location to multiple, potentially incompatible, descriptors. tldr: 该论文从理论上证明了位置编码器受Lipschitz约束其输出固有维度至多为2，并提出LoCA方法使位置编码器能够同时将单个位置映射到多个模态的描述符，从而实现多模态能力。
en_tdlr: This paper theoretically proves that location encoders are structurally limited to an intrinsic dimension of at most 2 due to Lipschitz constraints, and proposes LoCA to enable multi-modality by mapping a single location to multiple, potentially incompatible, descriptors.
